title: A score should never travel alone.
question: What happens to a reported evaluation result after the run, and which review states can Eval Evidence support?
takeaway: Eval Evidence binds a reported score to retained evidence so review can distinguish aligned conditions, differences, missing evidence, and changed bytes.

reading_speeds.at_2_seconds: A reported score moves through sealing and verification to explicit review states.
reading_speeds.at_20_seconds: The reader can follow the three-stage lifecycle and distinguish matched, different, unavailable, and integrity-failure outcomes.
reading_speeds.at_2_minutes: The retained evidence categories, proof limits, source map, accessibility contract, and deterministic provenance are inspectable.

medium.rationale: Exact evidence states, editable labels, accessible text, and reviewable proof boundaries are required.

labels.claim: A result enters the post-run evidence lifecycle with captured, asserted, derived, or unavailable evidence.
Bundle construction binds normalized claims and referenced-file digests; verification checks only the named integrity surfaces.
Review reports aligned conditions, material differences, missing evidence, or integrity failures without ranking models.
The recorded conditions being reviewed align.
The evidence needed for the comparison was not retained.
Referenced bytes no longer match the stored digest.
Model identity is one retained instrument field.
Harness identity is one retained instrument field.
Configured or observed budgets are retained with field provenance when available.
Verifier evidence remains distinct from the reported reward.
Selected referenced artifacts are bound by content digests.
Normalized evidence fields retain explicit status and source information.
The bottom annotation limits the adjacent lifecycle claims.

boundaries: Eval Evidence does not run evaluations or models.
Digest and reference checks do not establish physical truth or signer authenticity.
The visual does not reduce evidence to a universal trust, fairness, or model-ranking score.
forbidden_claims: Do not claim model ranking or comparative model quality.
Do not claim physical verification or authenticity.
Do not claim deployment, release, or adoption status.

accessibility.alt_text: A reported score moves through sealing and verification to matched, different, unavailable, or integrity-failure review states.
accessibility.long_description: A left-to-right post-run lifecycle starts with a reported score, binds recorded model, harness, budget, verifier, artifact, and field-provenance evidence, and then reports one of four explicit review states. A boundary note states that Eval Evidence does not run evaluations, establish physical truth, or issue a universal score.
